title: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping

claims.claim: Meta is delaying the enforcement of its new business terms to November 20th.

evidence.quote: Meta is delaying the enforcement of its new business terms after publishers raised concerns that they could allow the company to scrape news sites for AI training, as reported earlier by Fast Company. In a statement to The Verge, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts says the terms will go into effect on November 20th

claims.claim: The business terms were originally supposed to go into effect on October 30th.

evidence.quote: The business terms, which were originally supposed to go into effect on October 30th, appeared to give Meta permission to freely scrape the new sites that use its platforms

claims.claim: Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts stated the delay allows more time to explain changes to partners and stakeholders.

evidence.quote: In a statement to The Verge, Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts says the terms will go into effect on November 20th “to allow more time for us to explain to our partners and stakeholders what’s changing and what’s not.”

claims.claim: The News/Media Alliance sent a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on Thursday regarding the business terms.

evidence.quote: The News/Media Alliance sent a letter to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on Thursday, demanding that the company revise its business terms over concerns that they would cause “severe harm” to publishers.

claims.claim: Digital advertisers and publishers in the European Union and the UK urged regulators to force Meta to halt its new terms.

evidence.quote: Digital advertisers and publishers in the European Union and the UK also urged regulators to force Meta to halt its new terms.
